transcript: I kind of agree with what Gen is saying here, but I'm gonna counter a little bit. first though, If you haven't watched Gen's whole video, please do. Gen is one of my favorite theatre content creators. He's basically critiquing this trend of celebrity driven revivals that don't do or say anything interesting with the material. And I agree with several of the points he's making here, including the overcharging. Absolutely. The ticket prices are out of control. And I agree that the best revivals are the ones that have a fresh take on the material or where the material meets the moment. But I still think there's something to be said for just seeing the great actors of our time take on the great roles in the canon. I think there can be something very compelling about seeing that marriage of actor and role. And maybe this is where we disagree, but to me that's a sufficient reason for a revival to exist. I would even say some of the examples you gave, like Music Man and Othello on paper, could have been something really special for that reason. And as far as being reinvented or having a specific relevance for that moment, obviously that's ideal. But I also think we, the die hard theatre fans, have had many opportunities to see these famous, iconic works performed at a very high level. But that's not necessarily true of newer or more general audiences. I think the trend you're pointing out is real, but I would instead attribute it to the fact that those productions were just not very good. I say this all the time with jukebox musicals, too. I don't have a problem with the concept of a jukebox musical, artistically, I have a problem with greed and laziness. And just like you can have a really well executed jukebox musical, I think you can have a really well executed revival that's both traditional and star driven. In fact, I think there have been many across Broadway, off Broadway, West End, even when the play has been done quite recently, of course, Gen alluded to a 4th example that we’re maybe not naming by name. And I take issue with that revival too, but to me, it's because there's other contextual things around it that kind of reek of hubris.
classificationReason: Stitch/response video engaging with another creator's argument about celebrity-driven Broadway revivals in general. Music Man and Othello are mentioned only as trend examples — no first-hand review of any specific listed production.
